name: Total Chaos Pack
description: A spicier pack: geese with vendettas, viral fame, haunted inheritances, and suspiciously persuasive strangers at bus stops.

events.title: Goose encounter
events.description: A goose blocks your path, wings spread, screaming at a frequency only you can hear.

choices.result: You ran. The goose honked in triumph. Somewhere, it is still honking.

outcomes.result: You won the duel. The goose retreated — but it made a call. You saw it make a call.
The goose won decisively. You now have a mortal enemy with wings.
The goose accepted your tribute. You have been adopted by a goose. This is legally binding now.
The goose took the bread AND your dignity. Classic goose.

events.title: The goose remembers
events.description: You hear honking behind you. It has found you. It has been training.

choices.result: You escaped, barely. The goose let you go. It wants you to live with the fear.

outcomes.result: The goose accepted your apology with a single solemn honk. Peace, at last.
Your apology was deemed insufficient. The goose's lawyers will be in touch.

events.title: A gift from the goose
events.description: Your goose arrives with something shiny in its beak. It drops it at your feet and waits.

outcomes.result: It's a gold locket. The goose watches you sell it for $120. No judgment.
It's a bottle cap. It is now your most treasured possession.

choices.result: The goose seemed hurt. You will think about this at 3am.

events.title: Mystery meat
events.description: The cafeteria is serving something the lunch lady calls 'the special'. It is grey. It is moving, slightly.

outcomes.result: Surprisingly decent? You went back for seconds. The lunch lady respects you now.
You ate the special and felt nothing. Nothing can hurt you ever again.
Regret, served on a beige tray. You spent lunch in the bathroom reconsidering everything.

choices.text: Trade it for a pudding cup
choices.result: You flipped the special for two pudding cups and a juice box. Wall Street is calling.

events.title: Cafeteria food fight
events.description: Someone threw a tater tot. It has escalated. The principal is on the table. There are no rules now.

outcomes.result: You landed a mashed-potato spiral from across the room. Legend status achieved.
You threw tater tots with courage and distinction. Nobody will forget this. Unfortunately, that includes the principal.

choices.result: You survived, but at what cost? Everyone saw you hiding with the lunch monitors.

events.title: Detention
events.description: The principal's office. Fluorescent lights. A worksheet titled 'Reflection'. The door is... slightly ajar.

choices.result: You wrote 'I will not weaponize side dishes' 100 times. Worth it.

outcomes.result: You went out the window, commando-rolled into the hedges, and walked home a free child.
You got stuck in the window frame for 40 minutes. The custodian took a photo.

events.title: Substitute teacher
events.description: The substitute has given up by 9:15am. She's wheeling in the big TV cart. It's going to be that kind of day.

choices.result: You watched a documentary about volcanoes twice. A perfect day.
You did math while everyone else watched volcanoes. Your small act of rebellion.

events.title: The exam dream
events.description: You wake at 4am, certain you have an exam today. You check the calendar. You do not. Your body refuses to believe this.

choices.result: You studied for a fake exam. Somewhere a parallel-universe you just passed it.
You fell back asleep and dreamt you were a spoon. Better than the exam dream.

events.title: The pet rock
events.description: A kid at the swap meet is selling pet rocks. This one has a face painted on it. It is looking at you.

choices.result: You named it Sebastian. Sebastian never sheds, never barks, never leaves. Sebastian is forever.
You declined. The rock watched you leave. You will wonder about this.

events.title: Sebastian's graduation
events.description: You find Sebastian the pet rock at the back of a drawer. He has been with you through everything. He still has the face.

choices.result: Sebastian sits on your desk at work now. Coworkers ask questions. You answer none of them.
You placed Sebastian in a nice garden. Circle of life. You cried anyway.

events.title: Identity shopping
events.description: The mall demands you pick a personality. Three kiosks are eyeing you: Hot Topic, a skateboard shop, and the debate club recruitment table.

choices.result: Black eyeliner, black boots, black soul (affectionate). Your mom pretends not to notice.
You fell off the skateboard in the parking lot. Cool points: acquired anyway.
You learned to argue both sides of any issue. Your family now lives in fear of 'actually'.

events.title: Talent show
events.description: The annual talent show needs one more act. Your name was nominated. You did not nominate yourself.

outcomes.result: Your rendition of 'My Heart Will Go On' brought the gymnasium to its feet. A scout was present (allegedly).
The recorder betrayed you on the high note. The video is already on three phones.

choices.result: You coughed theatrically and were excused. The recorder remains unplayed. History is safe.

events.title: The forbidden locker
events.description: Locker 237 was supposed to be sealed in 1987. It's open. Inside: a faint humming sound and what appears to be a study hall that never ends.

outcomes.result: You spent what felt like a semester in there and emerged knowing the quadratic formula in your bones. Also, it was Friday the whole time.
You saw a vision of every future report card. You closed the locker and never spoke of it.

choices.result: You shut Locker 237 forever. Probably for the best. Probably.

events.title: You went viral
events.description: Someone filmed you falling directly into a fountain, standing up, and bowing. 4.2 million views. The internet has decided you are 'Fountain Guy/Gal'.

choices.result: You made a merch store within 48 hours. Fountain Guy/Gal is a brand now.
You scrubbed your accounts. The internet moved on within a week, as it does.

events.title: A brand reaches out
events.description: An energy drink called 'MAXIMUM CURRENT' wants to sponsor you. The contract is 40 pages long and glows faintly.

outcomes.result: You now drink MAXIMUM CURRENT on camera twice a week. Your teeth hum. You made $8,000.
The energy drink was discontinued after 'the incident'. Your sponsorship, and your fame, evaporated.

choices.result: You declined. MAXIMUM CURRENT sponsored a guy who juggles chainsaws instead. Fair enough.

events.title: The algorithm turns
events.description: Your views are down 80%. The comments have shifted from adoration to 'anyone else forget this person existed?'

outcomes.result: Your comeback video — you, a fountain, a choreographed routine — hit 10 million views. Redemption arc complete.
The stunt flopped so hard it became a case study. You are now famous in marketing textbooks, which is worse.

choices.result: You posted a graceful farewell. Three people cried. You were one of them.

events.title: Influencer beef
events.description: A rival content creator named Chad Thunder has released a 14-minute video dissecting your fountain fall frame by frame. It's oddly respectful. It's war.

outcomes.result: Your response was surgical. Chad Thunder now follows you. Brands threw $3,000 at the drama.
You got ratio'd so badly that three reply guys formed a book club about it.

choices.result: You ignored it. Chad Thunder declared victory over no one in particular.

events.title: The garage band
events.description: Two acquaintances and a guy named Soup want to start a band. They need a bassist. You do not play bass. Soup says 'it's basically a big guitar'.

choices.result: You're the bassist for 'Permanent Wednesday'. Practice is Thursdays and whenever Soup's mom is out.
The band broke up over a disagreement about the name before you even joined. Bullet dodged.

events.title: Battle of the Bands
events.description: Permanent Wednesday made the finals of the regional Battle of the Bands. The competition: four bands, one of which is literally a police cover band.

outcomes.result: Permanent Wednesday WON. You beat a police cover band in front of their own families. Prize: $2,000 and a trophy shaped like a guitar.
Soup broke a string, the drummer fell off the stool, and the police cover band played 'Bad Boys'. You placed fourth. There were four bands.
Their drum kit mysteriously lost a kick pedal, they played 22 minutes of rimshots, and Permanent Wednesday took the trophy. Nobody can prove anything.
You were caught loosening the kick pedal by an actual police officer who was IN the police cover band. The band kicked you out via unanimous vote.

events.title: A peculiar match
events.description: You've matched with someone whose profile is entirely pictures of lasagna. They message: 'I also enjoy lasagna.' This is going great.

outcomes.result: Turns out you're both delightful. You shared lasagna and life stories. You're together now — the lasagna posts were real.
They brought their own lasagna to the restaurant and critiqued the chef's. There will not be a second date.
No romantic spark, but they're now your lasagna dealer. An excellent trade.

choices.result: You unmatched. Somewhere, a lasagna-themed profile wonders what went wrong.

events.title: Uninvited
events.description: A wedding is happening at the venue next door. You can smell the catered food from here. The guests all assume you're with the other side.

outcomes.result: You ate 40 shrimp, gave a toast as 'cousin Dave', and slow-clapped at all the right moments. Flawless.
You met someone at the singles table who was ALSO crashing the wedding. A love story for the ages.
The maid of honor ran the seating chart like a forensic accountant. You were escorted out mid-shrimp.

choices.result: You made toast. It was fine. The shrimp would have been better.

events.title: The wallet
events.description: A fat wallet on the sidewalk. $340 in cash, an ID, and a photo of a small dog wearing sunglasses.

outcomes.result: The owner gave you $100 and the dog's business card. The dog is a regional influencer.
The owner cried happy tears. The dog in the photo nodded approvingly (in the photo). Karma filed.

choices.result: You pocketed $340. You threw the wallet in a mailbox like a coward-hero. It doesn't sit right.

events.title: The bus stop prophet
events.description: A man at the bus stop, wearing three watches, leans in: 'ZorpCoin. It's going to the moon. I have charts.' He does not show you the charts.

choices.result: You bought 4 million ZorpCoin for $500. The man's three watches all said different times. Ominous or auspicious.
You bought 40 million ZorpCoin. The man whispered 'brave' and boarded a bus going the wrong direction.
You declined. He nodded sagely, as if your refusal was also foretold.

events.title: ZorpCoin portfolio check
events.description: You open the exchange app with the physical tension of a diffusing a bomb. The chart looks like a cardiogram designed by a raccoon.

outcomes.result: YOU SOLD AT THE TOP. $40,000. The three-watches man was right about one thing, at least.
You cashed out $800. A small miracle in this economy of cartoon coins.
ZorpCoin is now worth exactly $0.03 total. You sold it to pay the app's withdrawal fee.

choices.result: You held. Your heart rate is now pegged to a coin named after a frog.

events.title: The printer again
events.description: The office printer is jammed. The error message reads 'PC LOAD LETTER'. Nobody knows what this means. It has never meant anything.

outcomes.result: You struck the printer with the flat of your palm and it whirred back to life out of fear. Coworkers applauded.
The printer spat a crumpled page at your feet like a glove thrown before a duel. This is personal now.

choices.result: The ticket was auto-closed with 'have you tried turning it off and on'. You had. IT knows. IT always knows.

events.title: The printer strikes back
events.description: During the all-hands meeting, the printer begins printing your browser history. Slide 4 of the presentation is just a search for 'can pigeons remember faces'.

choices.text: Stand up and take the blame like a legend

outcomes.result: You announced 'yes, I DID research whether pigeons hold grudges, and they DO'. The CEO found it hilarious. The printer has made peace.
Silence. A cough. Someone wrote 'pigeon truther' on your desk nameplate. The printer's vendetta is complete; it is at peace.

choices.result: You unplugged it mid-sentence. The last page to emerge was half a search for 'pigeon legal rights'. Everyone saw enough. The printer is defeated but so are you.

events.title: The great soup heist
events.description: Your labeled minestrone is missing from the break room fridge. Security footage exists. HR has been 'made aware'. A reckoning is at hand.

choices.result: You built a corkboard with red string. The culprit: the new intern, who 'thought labels were decorative'. Justice was tepid.
HR mediated a 'soup circle' reconciliation session. The intern cried. You got a voucher for one (1) soup.
You released the minestrone into the universe. Inner peace tastes like chicken broth.

events.title: Jury duty
events.description: You've been summoned for jury duty. The case involves a dispute over a sandwich. Both parties are extremely serious. Juror #4 brought knitting.

choices.result: The sandwich was ruled a sandwich. You did your civic duty and felt strangely taller.

outcomes.result: You told the judge you 'believe sandwiches can speak'. You were excused with record speed.
The judge found your enthusiasm 'admirable'. You served. You were foreperson. It ruled you.

events.title: The hustle
events.description: A friend pitches you a business: bottled 'concert air' sold to fans as memorabilia. 'The Eagles alone...' he trails off meaningfully.

outcomes.result: People actually bought the air. You made $2,400 selling premium vacuum-sealed atmosphere. Capitalism.
The bottles just contained regular garage air. Customers could tell, somehow. You lost $200 and one friend.

choices.result: You passed on air. The friend went on to sell bottled 'rain' instead. It also failed.

events.title: An envelope from the tax office
events.description: Official letterhead. The phrase 'routine audit'. Your hands are already sweating and you haven't opened it yet.

choices.text: Hire the guy with the visor ($2,000)
choices.result: The visor guy found three deductions named after animals. Audit closed. You're clean AND you have a guy now.

outcomes.result: You out-paperworked the audit. They sent a letter saying 'impressive'. This is the highest compliment a tax office can give.
You claimed your pet as a dependent. The audit disagreed. $8,000 in back taxes, pet status revoked.

events.title: The reading of the will
events.description: A great-uncle you met once at a funeral has left you his estate: a Victorian mansion on a hill. The lawyer adds, casually, 'there's a disclosure about the attic.'

choices.result: The mansion is yours. At night, the attic door opens by itself. Rent is $0 though.
You sold the haunted mansion for $85,000 to a couple who 'love character'. They have been warned. They remain excited.

events.title: Meet Reginald
events.description: The attic ghost introduces himself by moving your furniture three inches to the left. His name is Reginald. He died here in 1911 and has opinions about your decor.

outcomes.result: Reginald pays rent in Victorian gold sovereigns he 'misplaced' in 1903. $5,000 worth. Best roommate ever.
Reginald agreed to stop moving the furniture. He did NOT agree to stop sighing dramatically at 3am.

choices.result: The exorcist took one look at Reginald's library and they spent four hours discussing Romantic poetry. You're out $800 and the ghost stays.

events.title: A familiar stranger
events.description: A wild-eyed stranger grabs your arm: 'I'm you. From the future. We don't have much time — the geese—' They glance over their shoulder. 'Just listen.'

outcomes.result: The numbers hit. $60,000. The stranger winked, said 'don't thank me, thank us', and walked into traffic backwards. They were fine.
The numbers won nothing. 'Oh wait,' the stranger said, 'wrong timeline.' Then they bought a pretzel and left.

choices.result: 'Invest early, forgive faster, moisturize.' The stranger dissolved into a flock of pigeons. Solid advice though.

choices.text: Punch them (you never liked you anyway)
choices.result: You punched yourself, technically. The stranger anticipated this and wore padding. 'We always try that,' they sighed.

events.title: Space rock delivery
events.description: A meteor the size of a toaster crashes into your yard at 3am. It is warm. It smells faintly of burnt toast. The neighbors are pretending they didn't see it.

choices.result: The museum paid $120,000 and named it after you, sort of. 'The [Your Name] Adjacent Meteorite'. Immortality-ish.

choices.text: Keep it as a lawn ornament
choices.result: The meteor stays. Property values are either up or down depending on who you ask. Tourists take photos. You charge them $1.

events.title: The truth about pigeons
events.description: A neighbor corners you: 'Pigeons aren't real. They're government drones. The bobbing is them recharging. I have a newsletter.' He produces a newsletter.

choices.result: Issue 1: 'Where Do Birds Go at Night? (Nowhere. They're Off.)' You're in.
You declined. But now every pigeon does seem to be watching you. No. Stop that.

events.title: Lights over the reservoir
events.description: The newsletter was right about ONE thing. A disc-shaped craft hovers over the water, broadcasting a beam that sounds like smooth jazz. A ramp lowers.

outcomes.result: They showed you the galaxy and taught you three truths about the universe. One of them was a recipe for incredible chili.
You were probed. Politely, consensually, with advanced instruments, but probed nonetheless. They gave you a commemorative t-shirt.
Turns out they just wanted your streaming password — their planet has terrible content licensing. You gave them the guest profile.

choices.result: You ran. The ship played a sad trombone frequency and departed. The newsletter guy will never let this go.

events.title: The reunion
events.description: At the reunion, the kid who once demanded your lunch money approaches — older, calmer, holding a name tag that says 'Hi, I'm Sorry'.

choices.result: You shook hands. He teaches mindfulness now. The tater tot incident was addressed and healed.
You gave a 6-minute speech about 'the lunch money years'. The ballroom applauded. The bully nodded. Cinema.

events.title: Old acquaintance
events.description: The shady acquaintance from before resurfaces: 'One last job. Totally legal this time. Mostly.' He has a laminated business card now.

choices.result: You declined. He respected it — the business card was for a real paralegal's office. Character growth.

outcomes.result: It was actually mostly legal: recovering 'borrowed' vehicles. $9,000 for a weekend's work.
It was NOT mostly legal. Two years this time. The business card was fake. Of course it was.

events.title: Bingo night warfare
events.description: Community center bingo. Edna has won eleven weeks straight and it's not luck — it's a system. Tonight, you've brought your own lucky troll doll.

outcomes.result: B-7. BINGO. Edna's reign ends. $150 richer and a new legend is born.
Edna won again. She looked directly at you when she said it. The troll doll has been retired in disgrace.

choices.result: You played for fun and lost gracefully. Edna approved of you, which is its own victory.

events.title: The stunt challenge
events.description: Your friends are filming a stunt video: jumping a shopping cart over a shopping cart. They need someone 'aerodynamic'. They're looking at you.

choices.result: You declined. The shopping cart stunt proceeded without you and ended exactly how you predicted.

outcomes.result: You cleared it. The video is the crown jewel of the channel. Kids on bikes salute you now.
You did not clear it. The shopping cart is fine. You are mostly fine. The video has 2 million views.

effects.cause: an extremely ill-advised shopping cart stunt

outcomes.result: The physics were never in your favor.
